blocks.title: Sequence-ordered messaging model
blocks.text: MessagingGateway loads conversations and history, and RealtimeChannel delivers ServerEvent records that carry an inbox cursor and a per-conversation sequence. The outbox sends each draft with a clientMessageId; the thread store merges server messages by sequence and replaces pending entries by clientMessageId. Read positions, unread counts and history come from the server, while typing and presence stay short-lived hints.

blocks.title: Worked example: a reply sent during a reconnect

steps.title: Compose
steps.text: Ana writes in conversation cv_9 while the socket is live at inbox cursor 1203 and thread sequence 482. The outbox creates clientMessageId cm_17 and shows the reply as sending after the last confirmed message.

steps.title: Lose the network
steps.text: The connection fails during the POST. The request times out, the channel reports offline, and the bubble moves to retrying rather than failed, because the outcome is unknown.

steps.title: Reconnect
steps.text: The channel reconnects with backoff and asks for events after cursor 1203. The server returns message 483 from Ben and message 484, which carries cm_17 because the first POST had arrived.

steps.title: Reconcile
steps.text: The thread inserts 483 above the pending bubble, then matches 484 to cm_17 and replaces it. The outbox clears its retry because the id is confirmed, so no second copy reaches Ben.

steps.title: Read
steps.text: The thread is visible, so Ana's client sends read position 484. Ben's phone receives read.updated and shows that Ana has seen his message, without any client clock involved.

blocks.alt: Messaging flow where the composer sends with a client message id, the server assigns a sequence, and realtime events update the thread and inbox stores.
blocks.caption: Authority flow: the outbox carries intent, while order, read positions and history come back from the messaging backend.
blocks.fallbackText: Text fallback: The outbox posts a message with its clientMessageId. The backend assigns a sequence and emits events with an inbox cursor. The thread store orders by sequence, the inbox store updates counts, and read positions return as events.
